free_tier.stated: CPU - First 180,000 vCPU-seconds free per month ... RAM - First 360,000 GiB-seconds free per month ... Requests - 2 million requests free per month.

egress.terms: Outbound internet data transfer is charged at Google Cloud networking rates "with a free tier of 1GiB free data transfer within North America per month".; ingress: http-only
egress.free_allowance: Outbound internet data transfer is charged at Google Cloud networking rates "with a free tier of 1GiB free data transfer within North America per month".

interface_detail: gcloud CLI, REST API, and console.
chaining: Cloud Run can host an HTTP API; a WireGuard endpoint needs a VM, not a service.

limits.value: 1 GiB/month free data transfer within North America

binding_note: 1 GiB/month free transfer is 0.001 TiB; egress past it is billed at Premium tier rates. The transport fails before that.

identity_cost.detail: A Google Cloud billing account with a payment method; the free tier is a billing discount, not an account without a card.

reliability_note: Request timeout caps a stream; WebSockets must reconnect. Scale to zero adds cold starts.
confidence_note: Cloud Run publishes no page that says "UDP is not supported"; the conclusion follows from the container contract requiring an HTTP listener on one port, and from Google's own developer forum answer that it will not work with UDP. A first-party negative statement would raise this to documented.

evidence.proved: Free tier: 180,000 vCPU-s, 360,000 GiB-s, 2M requests; 1 GiB free data transfer within North America
"The ingress container within an instance must listen for requests on 0.0.0.0 on the port to which requests are sent."
"WebSockets streams are HTTP requests" subject to the request timeout
third party: the container contract requires an HTTP server, so UDP will not work

notes: Cloud Run also requires a card, so it fails identity for a no-card client even before the transport does. Included here because it is the most common answer to "where do I run this".

extras.wg_detail: No raw port. "The ingress container within an instance must listen for requests on 0.0.0.0 on the port to which requests are sent"; requests are HTTP, and WebSocket streams "are HTTP requests".
extras.volume_stated: Outbound internet data transfer is charged at Google Cloud networking rates "with a free tier of 1GiB free data transfer within North America per month".
extras.transit_note: Google's front end terminates HTTP and forwards requests.
